Looking at this question about RNA editing and alternative splicing in mouse retina cells, I need to recall research findings on the overlap between these two post-transcriptional modifications.

Studies examining RNA editing (primarily A-to-I editing by ADAR enzymes) in mouse retina cells have shown a significant co-occurrence with alternative splicing. The research indicated that a large majority of genes undergoing RNA editing in these cells also display alternative splicing events.

The specific finding from studies on mouse retina RNA editing is that approximately 73% of genes that undergo RNA editing also display alternative splicing.
